Application Materials.content:
When you apply you’ll need to submit a personal statement explaining why you want to take the course. You’ll need to include information about:
- your knowledge of the subject area
- why you want to study a postgraduate qualification in this course
- how you intend to use your qualification
References are not required for this programme. Please include the required paperwork showing your first degree and your IELTS English language test score (if you are a non-native English speaker) with your application. Without these, your application may be delayed.

Interview Requirements.content: If you don't have the exact entry requirements, but you have significant work experience in this sector we’ll assess your relevant professional experience, your subject knowledge and your aptitude for learning. Your application will be considered on individual merit and you may be asked to attend an interview.

Application Deadlines.content:
- Business Analytics and Finance (MSc) starts **September 2026** for **1 year**.
- International students: The deadline to apply for this course is **Wednesday 19 August 2026, midday UK time**. Applications may close before the expected deadline if places are filled.

Academic Requirements.content:
You’ll need a **2.1 degree** in a subject which includes quantitative study such as:
- finance
- sciences
- maths
- engineering
- computer science
- economics
- quantitative business or management
We do not accept the following subjects:
- Language Studies – degrees that focus on learning a language or how to translate, such as 'Business English', 'Applied English', or 'Translation', are not acceptable. However, this restriction does not apply to ‘English’ and ‘English literature’ degrees of the kind taught in the UK.
- Art/Design/Vocational Studies – degrees that focus on learning a particular form of art, craft or vocation. These include degrees in art, graphic design, photography, television broadcasting, script writing, or performance/dance.
This degree is ideal for those who have previously been exposed to other disciplines and fields which perhaps incorporated data analytics skills or quantitative subject, such as economics, mathematics, physics, engineering or computer science. It will also suit you if you have relevant professional experience.
If you don't have the exact entry requirements, but you have significant work experience in this sector we’ll assess your relevant professional experience, your subject knowledge and your aptitude for learning. Your application will be considered on individual merit and you may be asked to attend an interview.
For applicants from China: Southampton accepts bachelor's degrees (学士学位) from China. To apply, you'll usually need the equivalent of a **2:1** undergraduate degree from a highly ranked Chinese university, with a minimum average grade depending on institution tier. For this course’s 2:1 requirement, the Chinese equivalent entry grades are:
| Tier | GPA out of 4.0 | GPA out of 5.0 | Percentage (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier A | **2.8** | **3.5** | **70%** |
| Tier B | **3.1** | **3.88** | **75%** |
| Tier C | **3.25** | **4.06** | **80%** |
| Tier D | **3.7** | **4.63** | **88%** |
If your institution isn't listed, use the grades for **tier D**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
If English is not your first language, you must show that you can use English to the level required. [Visit our English language pages](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/studentadmin/admissions/admissions-policies/language.page) to find out which qualifications are accepted and how you can meet the requirements.
If you are taking the International English Language Testing System (IELTS), you must get at least the following scores:
| IELTS score requirements | |
| --- | --- |
| overall score | **6.5** |
| reading | **6.0** |
| writing | **6.0** |
| speaking | **6.0** |
| listening | **6.0** |
If you do not meet the English language requirements through a test or qualification, you may be able to meet them by completing one of the [pre-sessional English programmes](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/pre-sessional) before you start your course.
When applying, please include the required paperwork showing your first degree and your IELTS English language test score (if you are a non-native English speaker) with your application. Without these, your application may be delayed.

Program Overview.content:
Business Analytics and Finance (MSc) is a **Master of Science** course starting **September 2026** for **1 year**. It is a **full-time** course based at **Highfield** and awarded by the **University of Southampton**.
Data analysis has become a dominant force in the modern global business landscape, and industries are looking for data-literate professionals with strong decision making and analytics skills, as well as financial acumen. This course will equip you with technical data science skills and non-technical management skills, along with a deep understanding of the application of analytics within the context of financial management. You will develop an interdisciplinary understanding of the applications of analytics in a financial context through data collection, data visualization, statistical/pattern analysis, and data mining.
The degree is ideal for those who have previously been exposed to other disciplines and fields which incorporated data analytics skills or a quantitative subject, such as economics, mathematics, physics, engineering or computer science. It will also suit applicants with relevant professional experience who are contemplating either furthering their career or making a career change.
Modules are designed to meet the latest industry demands and course contents are reviewed by the [Business Advisory Board](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/cormsis/about/businessadvisory.page), which includes industry experts from organisations such as Rolls Royce, BT Openreach, Ford and Shell. Students also benefit from the expertise of the [Centre of Operational Research, Management Sciences and Information Systems (CORMSIS)](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/cormsis/), one of the country’s strongest analytics research groups. Learning is informed by specialist research, and students can personalise their studies with optional modules focusing on areas such as financial risk management, advanced analytics, simulation and revenue management.
A dissertation component is integrated as part of the programme. Students either choose a dissertation topic with the help and guidance of a supervisor, or apply to work on an industry project; if selected, the industry project becomes the dissertation topic. The course structure runs for a full 12 months: the first 9 months cover taught modules, with exams in January and May, followed by dissertation work from June to September.
Learning includes lectures and seminars, individual and group exercises, computer classes, private study and workshops. Students explore topics through exercises using real-world data, case studies and numerical problem solving, and can gain specialist experience using analytics, modelling, coding and programming software such as Excel, Python and Anylogic. Assessment methods vary between modules and may include examinations, individual coursework, group work and dissertation. Students are assigned a personal tutor and have access to a senior tutor.
[Dr Steffen Bayer](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/people/5xhjf7/doctor-steffen-bayer) is the lead for this course. He is an Associate Professor at the University of Southampton Business School and Programme Leader for the MSc Business Analytics and Finance and MSc Business Analytics and Management Science. His research focuses on health service planning, including stroke and renal care, human resource planning and technology-supported healthcare delivery.
The course is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)](https://www.aacsb.edu/). Facilities include [Business study spaces](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/facilities/business-study-spaces) and a [Financial laboratory](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/facilities/financial-laboratory), which provides experience using Bloomberg terminals to access real-world financial market data.
Graduates commonly work in sectors including consultancy, technology, business, public sector and finance. Careers directly related to this course include operational researcher, market researcher, management consultant, financial analyst, business analyst, data scientist, quantitative analyst, data analyst, risk manager and supply chain manager. Example job titles of Southampton MSc Business Analytics and Finance graduates include data analyst, investment analyst, business analyst, management trainee, business and credit analyst, business intelligence analyst, credit risk analyst, financial analyst, management consultant and market research assistant.
Job prospects for MSc Business Analytics and Finance graduates: **£33k Average professional salary**, **81% In a skilled profession or further study**, and **95% Graduate employment rate**. Example graduate job titles and job prospect statistics are taken from The Graduate Outcomes Survey, which gathers information about the activities and perspectives of graduates 15 months after finishing their course.

Curriculum.content:
**Business Analytics and Finance (MSc)** starts **September 2026** and runs for **1 year**. Course type: **Full-time**. Campus: **Highfield**.
On this master’s degree in Business Analytics and Finance, studies run for a full **12 months**. The first **9 months** cover taught modules. There are **2 sets of exams**, in **January** and in **May**. Students then work on the dissertation from **June to September**.
A dissertation component is integrated as part of this programme. For this module, students follow one of the following options:
- Choose a topic to write the dissertation about with the help and guidance of a supervisor.
- Apply to work on an industry project; if selected, this will be the topic of the dissertation.
For entry in academic year **2026 to 2027**, Year 1 modules:
Students **must study** the following modules:
- [**Corporate Finance and Investment**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6022)
- [**Credit Risk & Data Analytics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6556)
- [**Optimisation and Decision Modelling**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6046)
- [**Quantitative Research in Finance**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6008)
Students **must also choose from** the following modules:
- [**Advanced Analytics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6554)
- [**Corporate Valuation and Strategy**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6023)
- [**Dissertation (Analytics)**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6545)
- [**Financial Portfolio Theory**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6017)
- [**Forecasting**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6011)
- [**Introduction to Python**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6189)
- [**Portfolio Theory and Asset Pricing**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6142)
- [**Project Management**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6537)
- [**Revenue Management**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6146)
- [**Simulation**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6122)
- [**Summer Project**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6546)
The dissertation gives students the opportunity to apply skills developed during the programme to a challenging problem. Students may apply for a dissertation topic set by a company or organisation, based on a real challenge they are facing, or develop their own topic and focus on a question that interests them. Throughout the dissertation, students work closely with an academic supervisor; if the project is with an external organisation, they also work with a representative from that organisation.

Financial Aid.content:
Southampton Business School (MSc) Dean Scholarship (International): Scholarships of **£9,000** and **£5,000** are available to international students studying an eligible postgraduate master’s at the University of Southampton Business School, including [MSc Business Analytics and Finance](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/business-analytics-finance-masters-msc "MSc Business Analytics and Finance 8522 (1 year)"). If you have a 1st or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies you will get **£9,000**. If you have a 2:1 or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies you will get **£5,000**.
Eligibility: you must be an international student required to pay the oversees fees; have a conditional or unconditional offer to study an eligible course; achieve a 1st or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies to receive a **£9,000** award; achieve a 2:1 or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies to receive a **£5,000** award. Students coming from China must have studied at a [Tier A](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/international/entry-qualification-equivalencies/china/postgraduate-taught-tier-list "Chinese awarding institutions listed by tier") university. There are a further 100 awards of either £9,000 or £5,000, depending on applicant eligibility, for applicants coming from a [Tier B](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/international/entry-qualification-equivalencies/china/postgraduate-taught-tier-list "Chinese awarding institutions listed by tier") Chinese university; these scholarships will be issued on a first past the post basis with an additional eligibility requirement being that applicants in this category pay their tuition fee deposit by **15th January 2026**.
You do not need to apply to this scholarship. If you meet the eligibility criteria, we will award you this scholarship and let you know by email.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Applicants in possession of an unconditional offer of a place may request that it be deferred to the next intake. The University does not typically permit more than a single deferral. For postgraduate taught study, applicants can make a request via their online application portal and requests for deferral will typically be accepted where there are unforeseeable life events and circumstances outside of the applicants’ control.
Reasons typically accepted for deferral include:
- Bereavement due to the loss of a close family member - a parent, grandparent, guardian, sibling, son, daughter or a close personal friend.
- Serious illness and health problems.
- Victim of a natural disaster.
- Victim of conflict and political unrest that prohibits travel to the UK.
- Personal accident or injury of a significant nature.
- Child care responsibilities or caring responsibilities.
- Relevant work experience/placements/internships.
- Military service.
- Change of employment circumstances.
- Unforeseen ATAS delays.
- Unforeseen Visa delays.
Reasons not typically accepted for deferral include:
- Unsuccessful in securing funding (e.g. scholarship) except in cases of the Sanctuary Scholarship.
- To undertake employment or travel unrelated to the degree programme applied for.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you do not meet the English language requirements through a test or qualification, you may be able to meet them by completing one of the University of Southampton's [pre-sessional English programmes](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/pre-sessional) **before you start your course**.
If you don’t meet direct entry requirements, you can apply to complete a Pre-Master's programme through the University's partnership with OnCampus. You'll progress to your chosen course after successfully completing the programme. [Find out more about Pre-Master's programmes for international students.](https://www.oncampus.global/our-study-centres/oncampus-southampton/progression-degrees)
